touches.text: RECOVERY DEVICE (cairn/devices/recovery/; Recovery And Installation Manager: the host, install, upgrades, root, Rescue and trouble tickets)

A well designed tool should disappear in use: so little friction it's almost an extension of the user. Traditional software makes installing, opening and using it three separate tasks; Cairn makes them one command.
It operates when the bus is down, and when nothing is installed at all. The cairn command calls it directly.

Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).
`cairn start` (= cairn cairn start) brings the system up: ground loop, bus, shims. `cairn stop` takes it down.
Any cairn command brings up whatever it needs, including the whole install on the very first run (6.3.2). WHY: a well designed tool should disappear in use.

Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.
